Hi Vivek / Connor —

Thanks for the recap. We started running a couple of tests this morning and are hitting a consistent 500 when we call the /v1/rerank endpoint with a structured payload (we batch ~32 docs, payload ~900KB). Error looks like: 

{
  "error": "500 Internal Server Error",
  "message": "upstream error: connection reset by peer while routing"
}

Repro snippet we used (curl):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_abcxyz" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d @batch_rerank_payload.json -v

We attached the logs (integral-logs-20261110.zip). The logs include the request/response headers and a truncated body. We also noticed the SDK retries three times before returning the 500.

Any quick checks we should run? We tested both the SDK and straight curl; same behavior.

Appreciate the fast follow-up.

—Alex

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK handshake & payload triage

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the logs — I took a quick pass. A few hypotheses and immediate checks that help narrow this down: 

1) Payload size / routing buffer: you mentioned ~900KB. Some of our routing proxies previously had a default buffer that led to mid-request resets for >750KB JSON bodies in chunked flows. Quick check: retry the same curl but add a Content-Length header (avoid chunked transfer) or compress the payload (gzip) and set Content-Encoding: gzip.

2) Auth handshake: when using our SDK, verify token refresh works (refresh token flow) — if token refresh triggers during a multi-part request some SDKs open a new connection and that race can cause upstream resets. You can force a single-shot test with a long-lived token to rule this out.

3) Structured output / function-calling: if you are sending a large functions array or embedding requests inside structured_call fields, try sending a smaller batch (8 docs) and toggle the structured_call flag off to see if the request completes.

Minimal repro curl I used locally (works consistently with smaller payloads):

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer pk_live_TEST" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Model: reranker-v2" \n  -H "Content-Length: 34567" \n  --data-binary @small_batched_payload.json

Please run that and paste the verbose curl (-v) output if you still see the 500. I also attached a tiny repro curl and a quick checklist (redwood-quick-repro-curl.txt) to this thread.

If this is blocking you in production we can escalate to a routing hotfix; otherwise there’s a config workaround (gzip + shorter batches) you can apply immediately.

—Olga
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK handshake & payload triage

Thanks Olga — we ran the tests you suggested. Results: 

- Re-running with Content-Length set (no chunked): still returns 500, but different body: 
{
  "error": "502 Bad Gateway",
  "message": "upstream closed connection during body read"
}

- Sending the same batch gzipped and Content-Encoding: gzip: request succeeds (200) but latency is high (~2.6s) compared to smaller batches.

- Sending batches of 8 docs (uncompressed): succeeds consistently.

Attached: verbose curl outputs (redwood-quick-repro-curl.txt) and the unredacted verbose trace in the zip.

One more datapoint: the error only shows up when we send a structured_call payload that includes an embeddings array (we send both reranker inputs and embedded metadata together). If we strip the embeddings and call rerank only, large batches work.

We can apply gzip + batching as a short-term fix but would prefer a platform-side resolution — happy to jump on a call to coordinate.

—Alex

Subject: Re: Post-demo: SDK handshake & payload triage

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for validating those experiments and for the logs. Summary & plan: 

- Root cause (initial assessment): our router (Nginx layer in front of the cluster) is dropping connections when requests include both a large structured_call body and inline embeddings arrays. The router's upstream buffer and request-body read behavior can cause the upstream to close during body read, which produces the 502/500 patterns you saw.

- Immediate mitigations (you can apply now):
  * Continue using gzip + Content-Encoding: gzip for large batches.
  * Reduce batch size to 8–12 docs for reranker calls that include embeddings.
  * If using the SDK, set the env var REDWOOD_FORCE_NO_CHUNKED=1 (SDK v1.9.2+ will honor this and send a Content-Length).

- Short-term platform fix: we will push a routing config that increases request buffer sizes and adjusts proxy_read_timeout for rerank routes in hosted. This will be staged to dedicated customers first and rolled to hosted within 48 hours.

- Follow-up: propose a brief technical sync tomorrow at 9am PT to validate after we stage the config (I’ll send a calendar invite).

I’ll also open an internal ticket (INT-7809) to track the fix and link your logs. Vivek — can you confirm timing for the sync with Alex / Priya?

Thanks,
Connor
Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
